Consult Summary:
- Right knee pain with intermittent clicking and functional limitation developing over ~2 weeks after increasing running distance; associated transient right toe tingling after a run. Referral to physiotherapy and a prescription for a stronger anti-inflammatory planned; advised rest/ice and return precautions.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Right knee pain with clicking, worse with running and certain gym movements; reduced running tolerance.
  - One episode of tingling in right toes after a run.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptoms began approximately 2 weeks ago.
  - Began marathon training ~1 month ago with recent longer runs (up to 7–8 miles); knee pain typically begins ~20 minutes into a run (approximately 2.5–3 miles).
  - Initial swelling noted after first long run which resolved with ice; currently not swollen at rest.
  - Pain/clicking occurs with flexion/extension during gym activities and during longer runs; currently intermittent and sometimes resolves when not active.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Exacerbated by longer runs and specific gym movements requiring knee flexion/extension.
  - Improved with ice therapy.
  - Patient occasionally takes over-the-counter analgesics (ibuprofen) which she reports helps.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - No locking of the knee reported.
  - No sensation of the knee giving way/instability reported.
  - Full range of motion reported (able to fully straighten and flex).
  - No difficulty with walking normally or stairs.
  - No calf pain, no persistent erythema or warmth reported.
  - Intermittent mild lower-leg/ankle indentation from socks after prolonged standing (noted by patient).
  - No systemic symptoms (fever/malaise) reported.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No persistent swelling at present.
  - No persistent sensory deficit; toe tingling described as a single prior episode and resolved.
  - No reported color or temperature change of lower limb.

Past Medical History:
- Refractive error — farsighted; underwent LASIK.
- History of UTI with ED visit previously (one occasion; concern for kidney stones at that time).
- Otherwise reports usual minor illnesses (colds); no chronic musculoskeletal diagnoses reported.
- No prior described chronic joint problems.

Medications:
- Ibuprofen — patient reports taking up to approximately 400 mg as needed; dose/route/frequency not fully documented.
- Aleve (patient-reported; class uncertain to patient) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Vitamin D — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Melatonin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Xanax (occasional use) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Note: Provider offered to prescribe a stronger anti-inflammatory and stated it should not be combined with ibuprofen; prescription to be sent to pharmacy.

Allergies:
- No allergies reported / not documented.

Social History:
- Lives at home (address provided).
- Active lifestyle: regularly attends gym and plays sports including ice hockey.
- Marathon training in progress (current runs up to 7–8 miles; started training ~1 month ago; marathon scheduled in June).
- Recreational substance use: occasionally smokes a marijuana joint.
- Tobacco and alcohol use not documented.

Family History:
- Not discussed / not documented.

Physical Examination:
- No vital signs documented.
- No physical examination findings documented (no clinical exam performed during this consult).

Investigations:
- No imaging or laboratory investigations performed or reported.
- Plan discussed to consider imaging if indicated after physiotherapy assessment.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Right knee pain with clicking, likely related to increased training / overuse (definitive diagnosis not established via video consult)
  - Assessment: Mechanical knee symptoms (pain and clicking) developing over 2 weeks with activity; initial transient swelling after activity; full ROM and no reported instability or locking on history.
  - Plan:
    - Continue ice therapy as tolerated.
    - Reduce running volume / ease up on training; avoid running through pain.
    - Advise continuation of analgesia as needed; provider to send prescription for a stronger anti-inflammatory to pharmacy (counsel: do not combine with ibuprofen; take with food).
    - Arrange referral to physiotherapy for formal assessment and targeted management.
    - If physiotherapist assessment suggests, consider imaging (e.g., to assess cartilage/ligament) thereafter.
    - Offer clinic appointment for physician assessment sooner if physiotherapy wait is prolonged.
- Issue 2: Intermittent tingling in right toes (single episode after a run)
  - Assessment: One reported episode of toe tingling after activity; currently resolved.
  - Plan:
    - Monitor for recurrence or progression.
    - Report and seek review if tingling/numbness persists, worsens, or other neurological signs develop.
- Issue 3: Intermittent lower-leg/foot swelling after prolonged standing (sock indentation)
  - Assessment: Mild dependent edema noted by patient; not associated with pain or redness.
  - Plan:
    - To be assessed during physiotherapy/clinical assessment if persists or worsens.
    - No specific intervention documented during this consult.
- Urgent warning signs advised:
  - Seek urgent review if knee develops persistent swelling, heat, redness, high temperature, becomes locked (unable to bend/straighten), or if systemic illness develops.
- Administrative:
  - Provider to send anti-inflammatory prescription to patient’s pharmacy.
  - Provider to issue physiotherapy referral.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No vital signs documented.
  - No clinician physical examination findings documented.
  - No documented allergies explicitly stated (patient did not report).
  - Medication doses/routes/frequencies largely not documented (patient provided approximate ibuprofen dose only).
  - No imaging or objective tests performed.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Initial comment implied "knees" but patient later clarified primarily right knee is affected; conflict noted.
  - Patient uncertain about Aleve identity/class (stated she thought it might be acetaminophen) — patient uncertainty documented.
- Transcript quality:
  - Conversation was audible and coherent; history details obtained clearly. No significant background noise or inaudible segments noted.
